policy_title: Boost Life Sciences Innovation and Patient Control
stated: Labour will develop an NHS innovation and adoption strategy, including a plan for procurement and reformed incentive structures, to accelerate new technology and medicines into the NHS. They will maximise UK potential in clinical trials by making the process more efficient and accessible through the NHS app. The NHS app will also be transformed to put patients in control of their health, allowing management of medicines, appointments, and health needs, including access to performance information and medical guidelines.

source.quote: As part of Labour’s life sciences plan, we will develop an NHS innovation and adoption strategy in England. This will include a plan for procurement, giving a clearer route to get products into the NHS, coupled with reformed incentive structures to drive innovation and faster regulatory approval for new technology and medicines. Drawing on the strength of our National Health Service, Labour will also maximise our potential to lead the world in clinical trials. This means making the process more efficient and accessible, by speeding up recruitment and giving more people a chance to participate through the NHS app. Labour will therefore transform the NHS app, putting patients in control of their own health to better manage their medicine, appointments, and health needs. This will include giving performance information on local services, and notifications of vaccinations and health checks. Patients will be able to see the medical guidelines for the treatment they should get, to hold health services to account and understand what their choices are.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS healthcare access and capacity: accelerating new medicines/technologies reduces treatment gaps, streamlined clinical trials expand available therapies, and the NHS app improvements directly affect appointment management, medicines control, and access to care information — all core O3 indicators.

Maximising UK potential in clinical trials by making the process more efficient through the NHS brings investment, high-value employment, and competitive advantage in a sector worth ~£94bn to the UK economy — a real, non-negligible prosperity effect beyond the healthcare goal.

membership_note: Two fundamentals bear materially: O3 for direct improvements to NHS access and care quality, and O13 for the economic/productivity opportunity in life sciences and clinical trials. The NHS app patient-control aspect enhances convenience and information access but does not change state coercive powers in a way that clears the O10 bar; any distributional effects are too indirect to reach O14.
